Hi Alex — thanks for the snapshot, that helps a lot. Quick summary of our recommended first-pass approach so we can align before the tech walkthrough: 

1) Batching: target continuous batching with a 10–25ms accumulate window during steady-state. For burst protection, we'll use adaptive micro-batching (max batch size 64 for classifier, 16 for chat) with immediate flush on explicit interactivity signals. Expected token-cost reduction: ~15–22% from batching alone on your traffic mix.

2) KV/prefix caching: since your templates are shared across tenants we recommend a two-tier cache: (a) prefix-level KV cache for static system+instruction prompts (high hit rate, cheap), (b) user-level short-term cache for repeated payloads (TTL 60s). We'll avoid cross-tenant cache merging; cache keys scoped by tenant id. This should cut repeated token serialization on chat histories by ~18–25%.

3) Quantization profiles: attach a short note with safe defaults. For the classifier (shorter sequences) we recommend int8 dynamic Q* for first rollout (profile A). For chat (long-context), start with fp16->int8 dual-path where long-attention stays fp16 for early canary, then progressively enable 4-bit quant on warm models (profile B). We'll document quality checks (per-prompt BLEU/ROUGE proxies + thresholded hallucination heuristics).

4) Routing and fallbacks: primary routing to a cost-optimized variant (quant profile A/B) with fast-failover to an fp16-compatible instance in another pool if p95 latency exceeds 125ms or error rate > 0.8%. We'll also set up a canary rollout window (2% traffic for 48h) with automated rollback triggers.

5) Metrics & evals: track token/unit costs, p50/p95 latency, model-level quality regression on the pre-approved prompt set, and cache hit ratio. We suggest daily automated evals and an hourly smoke check during the first 72h of canary.

Next step: 30-min tech walkthrough — can you do Monday 08/31 at 10:00am PT? I'll bring Monica (implementation lead) and Grace (profiling/quant lead).

Thanks,
